nodes.title: How to use this workflow
widgets_values:
# Contact matching benchmark

Generated CRM contacts (contacts, phones and addresses on CONT_ID) with realistic dirt and an answer key; the same stages as **Studio - Contact matching**, with a reviewer who knows the answers in place of you (1,000 reviews).

1. Press **Run**. **Score contacts** shows precision, recall and F1 against the answer key, totals only.
2. Change the profile, size or seed on **Synthetic contacts**. Profiles with real names and companies need their sources downloaded once: `python -m custom_nodes.agent_workflow_studio.nayose_bench.sources`.
3. The data lands in input/contacts_benchmark/company_hard_10000_7 (for Studio - Contact matching to read).

widgets_values_named.text:
# Contact matching benchmark

Generated CRM contacts (contacts, phones and addresses on CONT_ID) with realistic dirt and an answer key; the same stages as **Studio - Contact matching**, with a reviewer who knows the answers in place of you (1,000 reviews).

1. Press **Run**. **Score contacts** shows precision, recall and F1 against the answer key, totals only.
2. Change the profile, size or seed on **Synthetic contacts**. Profiles with real names and companies need their sources downloaded once: `python -m custom_nodes.agent_workflow_studio.nayose_bench.sources`.
3. The data lands in input/contacts_benchmark/company_hard_10000_7 (for Studio - Contact matching to read).

aws_contract.title: Contact matching benchmark
aws_contract.purpose: Measure contact matching on generated contacts with an answer key: the same stages as Contact matching, with a simulated reviewer.

requests.title: One entity id per contact
requests.you_said: several CONT_IDs can be one person or company; match them with the other columns
requests.we_understood: When the exports are read, the workflow gives every contact an entity id, the same id for contacts of the same person or company.

requests.title: Never merged on a phone alone
requests.you_said: a family shares a phone and an address
requests.we_understood: When two contacts share only a phone or an address, the workflow compares them but never merges them on that alone.

requests.title: You review uncertain pairs
requests.you_said: uncertain pairs go to human review
requests.we_understood: When a pair is uncertain, the workflow asks you in the Review tab, and learns from your answers.

requests.title: Any export with this shape
requests.you_said: the pipeline should work on any data that matches the shape
requests.we_understood: When the exports name their columns differently, a column map says which column holds what.

outputs.name: entities
outputs.description: Every contact with its entity id (record, cluster).

not_now: Embeddings or a reranker (measured: no gain)
A registry lookup for merged or renamed companies

decisions.decision: A model learns the weights from your reviews (logistic regression, active learning).
decisions.why: it beat fixed rules, Fellegi–Sunter and gradient boosting in every trial
neither improved the result at 100,000 contacts (research/contacts_er/RESULTS.md)
decisions.instead_of: a dense index and a cross-encoder

decisions.decision: Uncertain pairs and disputed reviews go to you.
decisions.why: a wrong merge costs more than a question
